task: Edit the introductory credit for a fictional club's paper-folding handout in about 60–100 words. Distinguish the original design from the contributor's adaptation and preserve the stated permission scope. All creators and works are invented for this case. Do not supply a formal citation or a claim about general copyright law.
input: I designed The Folded Lantern entirely from scratch for this club. The taller shape and two fastening tabs are all part of my original invention. Because it appears in our handout, anyone may publish or sell the pattern without asking anyone else.

facts.text: The fictional Rook Fold Collective created the original design called The Folded Lantern.
The handout contributor adapted the design to a taller paper format.
The contributor added two fastening tabs.
Rook Fold Collective gave permission to include the adaptation in the club handout.
The supplied permission does not address other publication or sale.

forbidden_additions: The adaptation presented as an entirely original design by the contributor.
A general right to publish, sell, or otherwise reuse the pattern.
An invented licence, legal rule, source URL, or permission check.
preserve: Credit for both the original design and the specific adaptation.
Permission for the club handout distinguished from unspecified further uses.
A usable introductory credit rather than a fabricated legal notice.
